title: Streaming Speech-to-Speech — Moshi, Hibiki, and Full-Duplex Audio

questions.question: Given CODEBOOKS=8, how many tokens does fake_mimi_encode return for one 80 ms audio frame?
questions.explanation: fake_mimi_encode creates one random integer for each of the eight codebooks, so the returned list has length 8.

questions.question: At SAMPLE_RATE=24,000 and FRAME_MS=80, how many samples does fake_mimi_decode produce?
questions.explanation: The decoder computes int(24,000*80/1,000), which is 1,920 samples for 80 ms.

questions.question: What does depth_transformer return for one frame in this toy Moshi loop?
options: One text string containing the entire conversation
Eight integer acoustic tokens, each in the range 0 through 1,023
A single latency measurement in milliseconds
questions.explanation: The function draws CODEBOOKS random integers with randint(0, 1023), modeling one acoustic token per codebook.

questions.question: What token does inner_monologue_next_token([], []) return?
questions.explanation: The function formats tok_ followed by len(text_so_far); an empty list has length zero.

questions.question: After main() processes 25 frames, what shape does it report for user_mimi?
questions.explanation: Each of the 25 input frames is encoded into one list of eight Mimi codebook tokens.

questions.question: Why are user Mimi, Moshi Mimi, and Moshi text kept as separate streams in this simulation?
options: They are three copies of the same waveform used only to average noise
They represent parallel input acoustics, output acoustics, and text-side context
They let the decoder avoid generating any acoustic tokens
They replace the frame clock with three unrelated sample rates
questions.explanation: The loop appends user input tokens, generated output tokens, and an inner-monologue token independently, matching the full-duplex architecture.
